{"key":"N1-313","summary":"Ticket watch: capture tracker responses in a PostToolUse hook, not model-relayed Writes","description":"## Problem

Ticket watch (N1-89) relays every tracker read through the model. The skill calls a jcm read tool, the model then `Write`s the "raw response" to `$N1_HOME/memory/<ID>/.tw-*.json`, and a shell helper parses that file. The file hop exists to keep tracker text out of shell strings (SEC-1), but it has two costs:

1. **Cost.** Each check takes 3 sequential Opus turns (MCP call → Write → Bash) at 130-250K context each. Ticket watch is **~9% of main-session tokens per run (median)** and **12-21% on 2026-11-03** (10-23 turns per run). It switched on across projects on 2026-10-29, when N1-178 backfilled `getChangelog`.
2. **Fidelity defect.** The model does not copy the response verbatim. Measured on N1-30x runs: `jcm_getIssue` and `jcm_getIssueChangelog` results of ~7.5-8K chars were written as 33-1,325 chars. `n1_tw_delta` therefore compares a hand-trimmed copy, so external comments or field changes can be dropped silently.

## Proposed approach (best practice: keep intermediate tool results out of the model)

- Add a `PostToolUse` hook for the jcm read tools that ticket watch uses (`jcm_searchIssues`, `jcm_getIssue`, `jcm_getIssueChangelog`, `jcm_getCurrentUser`). The hook writes `tool_response` byte-for-byte to the destination file. N1 already reads `tool_response` in `hooks/pr-review-observe.sh`.
- Destination: the procedure's shell step records the expected capture (tool name + dest path) in a marker file. The hook writes only when a marker for this session matches, then removes it. No model text reaches a shell (SEC-1 still holds).
- `procedures/ticket-watch.md` drops every "write the raw response to M/.tw-*.json" step. The MCP call is followed directly by the existing `n1_tw_*` helper.
- If the marker is missing or the capture file is absent, the helper fails closed the same way it does today ("seed failed, watch off" / no-op).

## Conditional scope

If the hook generalizes cleanly, apply the same capture to the other relay writes of model-held tracker text: `.desc-pre.*` / `.guard-live.*` (desc-hash-chain), queue `desc/*.title|.txt`. **Out of scope:** `review-hdr.md` and `fp-new.tsv`, which carry model-authored text rather than a tool response.

## Acceptance criteria

- Before implementing, a probe confirms the PostToolUse `tool_response` shape for an MCP tool on the installed Claude Code version. The finding is recorded in the ticket. (The docs summary says the field exists; its MCP shape is unverified.)
- Ticket-watch seed, check and CHANGED paths make no model `Write` call. Telemetry or transcript shows 0 `.tw-*` Writes on a live run.
- The file the helpers read equals the MCP tool result byte-for-byte. A test feeds a hook payload and diffs the output.
- With no marker, the hook writes nothing (other jcm calls are untouched).
- `tests/test_host_neutral_skills.sh` still passes, and skill text names no host tool.

## Evidence

Investigation 2026-11-03, scripts in `~/.n1/n1-plugin/scratch/orchestrator-writes-20261103/` (`twcost.py`, `attrib.py`, `sess.py`).

Sources: Anthropic, "Code execution with MCP" (intermediate results stay out of context); Claude Code hooks reference (PostToolUse `tool_response`, `updatedToolOutput`).","status":"In Progress","type":"Bug","parent":null,"priority":"High","assignee":"Vladimir Karnaukhov","reporter":{"displayName":"Vladimir Karnaukhov","accountId":"acct-redacted"},"labels":["n1-auto"],"updated":"2026-11-03T17:43:49.291+0300","updatedJql":"2026-11-03 17:43","comments":[{"id":"10855","author":"Vladimir Karnaukhov","authorAccountId":"acct-redacted","body":"**N1 design summary (N1-313)**

N1-314 (PR #257) already shipped `hooks/ticket-watch-capture.sh` and the HTTP check/seed path, so scope is narrowed to what remains:

1. Probe the real PostToolUse `tool_response` shape for jcm MCP tools on the installed Claude Code (AC1); record the finding here.
2. Prove byte-for-byte capture with a `cmp` test; drop the re-serializing `tojson` branch if the probe shows text blocks (AC3).
3. Capture `jcm_getCurrentUser` into `.tw-me.json` so the model no longer writes it on the Seed fallback.
4. Test the "nothing written" gates: no active run, other session, cursor present, subagent (AC4; the shipped hook has no marker, the gate chain gives the equivalent guarantee).
5. Host-neutral skill test stays green (AC5).

Out of scope: the desc-hash-chain and queue `desc/*` extension (model-extracted fields, queue session ownership, exact-string wiring tests). It goes to a linked follow-up ticket.

AC2 (0 `.tw-*` Writes on a live run) can only be measured after merge on the first live runs.","created":"2026-11-03T17:43:04.700+0300","updated":"2026-11-03T17:43:04.700+0300"}],"attachments":[]}
